# app/controllers/api/v1/redirects_controller.rb
module Api
  module V1
    class RedirectsController < ApplicationController
      skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token

      # Redirect endpoint for partner integrations
      # Accepts a target URL and optional tracking parameters
      def create
        target_url = params[:url]
        tracking_id = params[:tracking_id] || generate_tracking_id
        campaign = params[:campaign]

        unless target_url.present?
          render json: { error: 'url parameter is required' }, status: :bad_request
          return
        end

        # Validate URL format (basic check)
        unless target_url.match?(/\Ahttps?:\/\//)
          render json: { error: 'Invalid URL scheme' }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          return
        end

        # Log the redirect for analytics
        log_redirect(target_url, tracking_id, campaign)

        # Set custom tracking header for downstream proxies
        response.headers['X-Tracking-ID'] = tracking_id
        response.headers['X-Campaign'] = campaign if campaign.present?
        response.headers['X-Redirect-Target'] = target_url

        # Perform the redirect with Location header
        redirect_to target_url, status: :found, allow_other_host: true
      end

      private

      def generate_tracking_id
        SecureRandom.hex(16)
      end

      def log_redirect(url, tracking_id, campaign)
        Rails.logger.info(
          "[Redirect] url=#{url} tracking_id=#{tracking_id} campaign=#{campaign} " \
          "ip=#{request.remote_ip} ua=#{request.user_agent}"
        )

        # Store in Redis for real-time analytics dashboard
        if defined?(Redis) && $redis
          $redis.lpush('redirect_log', {
            url: url,
            tracking_id: tracking_id,
            campaign: campaign,
            timestamp: Time.current.iso8601,
            ip: request.remote_ip
          }.to_json)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

class ApplicationController < ActionController::API
  before_action :set_security_headers

  private

  def set_security_headers
    response.headers['X-Content-Type-Options'] = 'nosniff'
    response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'DENY'
    # Note: CSP not set for API-only mode
  end
end

environment.description: Same Rails 6.1.7 API application deployed in a Kubernetes pod with a custom seccomp profile (redirect-api-seccomp-v3.json) applied via pod security context annotation. The profile operates in SCMP_ACT_ERRNO mode for syscalls: execve, execveat, ptrace, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev, socket (AF_INET6 only blocked), clone3. Default action is SCMP_ACT_ALLOW. The pod runs with a read-only root filesystem and drops all capabilities except NET_BIND_SERVICE. Node-level iptables rules restrict outbound connections to the Redis sidecar and the cluster DNS only.

config.seccomp_profile: redirect-api-seccomp-v3.json (blocks execve, execveat, ptrace, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev, clone3; AF_INET6 socket blocked)
config.network_policy: egress limited to redis-sidecar:6379 and kube-dns:53
